nodes.label: Graphical Excellence
nodes.description: Well-designed presentation of interesting data—a matter of substance, of statistics, and of design. Consists of complex ideas communicated with clarity, precision, and efficiency.

nodes.label: Graphical Integrity
nodes.description: Telling the truth about the data. Avoiding distortion and deception in visual representation.

nodes.label: Lie Factor
nodes.description: The ratio of the size of the effect shown in the graphic to the size of the effect in the data. Should be around 1.0.

nodes.label: Data-Ink Ratio
nodes.description: The proportion of a graphic's ink devoted to the non-redundant display of data-information.

nodes.label: Chartjunk
nodes.description: Non-data-ink or redundant data-ink that clutters the graphic and distracts the viewer. Includes moiré effects, heavy grids, and 'ducks'.

nodes.label: Small Multiples
nodes.description: A series of similar graphics or charts, using the same scale and axes, allowing them to be easily compared.

nodes.label: Data Density
nodes.description: The number of data points per square inch. High data density graphics are usually better.

nodes.label: Multifunctioning Graphical Elements
nodes.description: Graphical elements that can convey data information and also perform a design function (e.g., forming a grid).
